title: AVERAGE vs AVERAGEA (and COUNT vs COUNTA): the A matters
meta_desc: AVERAGE vs AVERAGEA and COUNT vs COUNTA: how text and TRUE/FALSE cells silently change your numbers. Verified behavior across Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice.
intro: The A-suffix functions treat non-numeric cells as values (text counts as 0, TRUE as 1) instead of skipping them. That's occasionally what you want and more often a silent way to drag an average down with "N/A" strings.

cols: Counted as 0 — drags the average down
Universal — all verified in every version we test

when.use_when: Numeric statistics — placeholder text and flags shouldn't move the result. This is the right default.
COUNTA is the everyday one: counting filled cells of any type (list lengths, response counts). AVERAGEA is rare — only when text genuinely means zero, e.g. scoring sheets where "absent" scores 0.

compat_note: All four behave identically in every LibreOffice build and in the Google Sheets run we execute (Excel per Microsoft's docs — we do not run Excel). The subtle cross-check: if AVERAGE and AVERAGEA disagree on a range, that range contains text or booleans — a quick way to detect polluted numeric columns (=COUNTA(rng)-COUNT(rng) counts the non-numeric cells).

examples.label: How many cells are filled (any type)
